lines.text: How long to fall through the Earth? Down, down, and out the other side.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ tə fˈɔːl θɹuː ðɪ ˈɜːθ? dˈaʊn, dˈaʊn, ænd ˈaʊt ðɪ ˈʌðɚ sˈaɪd.

lines.text: Picture a tunnel through the middle: no air, no heat. It's about twelve thousand seven hundred kilometers. Driving it nonstop at highway speed takes about five days. You'll be falling.
lines.phonemes: pˈɪktʃɚɹ ɐ tˈʌnəl θɹuː ðə mˈɪdəl: nˈoʊ ˈɛɹ, nˈoʊ hˈiːt. ɪts ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛlv θˈaʊzənd sˈɛvən hˈʌndɹɪd kˈɪləmˌiːɾɚz . dɹˈaɪvɪŋ ɪt nˌɑːnstˈɑːp æt hˈaɪweɪ spˈiːd tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt fˈaɪv dˈeɪz. juːl biː fˈɔːlɪŋ.

lines.text: Gravity pulls you down, faster and faster. By the center: about ten kilometers a second. Then it slows you, and you reach the far side just as you stop.
lines.phonemes: ɡɹˈævᵻɾi pˈʊlz juː dˈaʊn, fˈæstɚɹ ænd fˈæstɚ. baɪ ðə sˈɛntɚ: ɐbˌaʊt tˈɛn kˈɪləmˌiːɾɚz ɐ sˈɛkənd. ðˈɛn ɪt slˈoʊz juː, ænd juː ɹˈiːtʃ ðə fˈɑːɹ sˈaɪd dʒˈʌst æz juː stˈɑːp.

lines.text: The textbook answer was forty-two minutes. It assumed Earth is equally dense all the way down. Then a graduate student, Alexander Klotz, used the real Earth. The core is so dense that gravity gets stronger before it fades.
lines.phonemes: ðə tˈɛkstbʊk ˈænsɚ wʌz fˈɔːɹɾitˈuː mˈɪnɪts. ɪɾ ɐsˈuːmd ˈɜːθ ɪz ˈiːkwəli dˈɛns ˈɔːl ðə wˈeɪ dˈaʊn. ðˈɛn ɐ ɡɹˈædʒuːət stˈuːdənt, ˌælɪɡzˈændɚ klˈɑːts , jˈuːzd ðə ɹˈiːəl ˈɜːθ. ðə kˈɔːɹ ɪz sˌoʊ dˈɛns ðæt ɡɹˈævᵻɾi ɡˈɛts stɹˈɔŋɡɚ bᵻfˌɔːɹ ɪt fˈeɪdz.

lines.text: His answer: about thirty-eight minutes. With nothing to stop you, you'd fall back and forth, a round trip every seventy-six minutes, forever.
lines.phonemes: hɪz ˈænsɚ: ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːɾiˈeɪt mˈɪnɪts. wɪð nˈʌθɪŋ tə stˈɑːp juː, juːd fˈɔːl bˈæk ænd fˈɔːɹθ, ɐ ɹˈaʊnd tɹˈɪp ˈɛvɹi sˈɛvəntisˈɪks mˈɪnɪts, fɚɹˈɛvɚ.

lines.text: Show your work. Make the core ten percent lighter: about thirty-nine. Make Earth uniform: forty-two.
lines.phonemes: ʃˈoʊ jʊɹ wˈɜːk. mˌeɪk ðə kˈɔːɹ tˈɛn pɚsˈɛnt lˈaɪɾɚ: ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːtinˈaɪn. mˌeɪk ˈɜːθ jˈuːnɪfˌɔːɹm: fˈɔːɹɾitˈuː.

lines.text: So those four missing minutes? They're the pull of Earth's heavy core.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ ðoʊz fˈɔːɹ mˈɪsɪŋ mˈɪnɪts? ðeɪɚ ðə pˈʊl ʌv ˈɜːθz hˈɛvi kˈɔːɹ.

lines.text: Next envelope: could all eight billion of us stand in one city?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: kʊd ˈɔːl ˈeɪt bˈɪliən ʌv ˌʌs stˈænd ɪn wˈʌn sˈɪɾi?
